verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled for launch no earlier than April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT)" (R1); "NASA Now Targeting April 1 for Artemis II's Launch" (R1); "Artemis II (April 1–11, 2026)" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm the launch was scheduled for and occurred on April 1, 2026, after delays, matching 'no earlier than' precisely.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send four astronauts on a 10-day crewed flyby around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Crewed lunar flyby mission... approximately 10-day trip" (R1); "four astronauts on a lunar flyby... 9 days, 1 hour" (R1); "10-day mission" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state four astronauts on ~10-day crewed lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the lunar vicinity since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972" (R1); "first crewed mission to the moon in more than half a century" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated in sources as first crewed to lunar vicinity since Apollo 17 (1972).

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft" (R1); "crew flight test... Orion spacecraft" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm it as first crewed test of Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "second flight of the Space Launch System (SLS)" (R1); "first crewed test flight of SLS and Orion" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as test/second flight of SLS with crew.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled for launch in early April 2026 from NASA's Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 1, 2026... Kennedy, LC-39B" (R1); "Launch Complex 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Launch on April 1 (early April) from Kennedy LC-39B confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II duration is approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "approximately 10-day Artemis" (R4); "9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes" (R1); "10-day mission" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as ~10 days.

verifications.claim: Reid Wiseman is the Commander of Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "commander Reid Wiseman" (R1); "Commander: Reid Wiseman" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm Wiseman as commander.

verifications.claim: Victor Glover is the Pilot of Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "pilot Victor Glover" (R1); "Pilot: Victor Glover" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation.

verifications.claim: Christina Koch is a Mission Specialist of Artemis II from NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "mission specialist Christina Koch... NASA Astronaut Corps" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match.

verifications.claim: Jeremy Hansen is a Mission Specialist of Artemis II from the Canadian Space Agency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "mission specialist Jeremy Hansen from the Canadian Astronaut Corps" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will feature Victor Glover as the first Black man to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Victor Glover (an African-American) became the first person of color... beyond low Earth orbit" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will feature Christina Koch as the first woman to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Christina Koch the first woman... beyond low Earth orbit" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will feature Jeremy Hansen as the first non-American to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen... beyond low Earth orbit" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II objectives include testing life support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "evaluated life support and other critical spacecraft systems" (R1); "test essential life support systems" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly part of objectives.

verifications.claim: Artemis II objectives include demonstrating the capability to navigate deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "manually controlling the spacecraft to evaluate its performance in deep space" (R1); "proximity operations demonstration" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Manual piloting and navigation tests in deep space directly support.

verifications.claim: Artemis II objectives include preparing for future Artemis III moon landing missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Stated as primary goal ahead of future landings.

verifications.claim: Artemis I successfully completed an uncrewed flight test in 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "uncrewed Artemis I mission in November 2022" (R1); "Artemis I (November 16, 2022)" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Confirmed successful uncrewed test in 2022.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a crewed lunar flyby scheduled for 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "crewed lunar flyby mission... 2026" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Direct description.

verifications.claim: Artemis III and beyond aim to land the first woman and next man on the Moon.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "When the programme began, one of its primary goals was to land the first female astronaut" (R9); earlier plans for Artemis III (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Was an initial aim for Artemis III, but program updated to Artemis IV for first landing; still program goal beyond.

verifications.claim: Artemis III and beyond target the lunar South Pole to establish a long-term presence
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "targeting the lunar South Pole region" (R2); "Moon's South Pole" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently targeted for south pole and long-term presence.
